findings.premise: Identity precedence and retention follow the resolved upstream decisions.
findings.evidence: HLD meta.questionResolutions selects one connected provider identity, repository Git email for multiple identities, and OS fallback; it requires private local retention until explicit learner deletion without automatic expiry. Sections 3.1 and 3.6 preserve those decisions. [files: .insrc/artifacts/HLD-670419c4ad8bea8e.json]

findings.premise: GraphStore currently opens 27 named databases with MAX_DBS=32.
findings.evidence: Read the complete getGraphStore initialization: its store literal opens 27 named databases, and MAX_DBS is 32. Adding eight requires capacity for 35; raising the limit to 64 addresses this. [files: src/db/graph/store.ts]

findings.premise: Existing IPC streaming supports progress/data events, request-ID substitution, explicit terminal frames and disconnect cancellation.
findings.evidence: handleStreamMessage writes '{ ...msg, id: request.id }', aborts on socket close/error, and does not send done when the handler resolves. IpcStreamMessage.data is unknown and its kind includes progress, done and error. [files: src/daemon/server.ts, src/shared/types.ts]

findings.premise: The five understanding roles are new registrations that can reuse existing role routing and floor enforcement.
findings.evidence: The complete role registry contains none of the five proposed roles. resolveRoleInternal uses descriptor.defaultTier and applyCoreFloor for registered roles; absent descriptors fall back to UNKNOWN_ROLE_TIER='mid' without floor protection. The proposed initialization guard addresses that fallback. [files: src/config/role-taxonomy.ts, src/analyze/context/role-router.ts, src/config/core-floor-guard.ts]

findings.premise: The watch lifecycle integration is sufficiently specified to deliver final unavailable/done frames during deliberate daemon shutdown.
findings.evidence: IpcServer.close only calls server.close; it neither signals active handlers nor closes their sockets. Daemon shutdown invokes 'void server.close()' and subsequently closes stores and exits. The LLD promises final shutdown frames but does not specify a subscription shutdown hook or its ordering in this existing lifecycle. [files: src/daemon/server.ts, src/daemon/index.ts, src/daemon/shutdown.ts]
findings.action: Specify an understanding-service shutdown hook in daemon/index.ts, invoke it before closing storage, and define how final frames are flushed before process exit. Add a shutdown-with-active-watch test.

findings.premise: Assessment versioning should be additive and independent of graph schema migration.
findings.evidence: GraphStore opens named databases within one root and separately checks its graph schema version before running graph migrations. HLD explicitly requires 'assessmentSchemaVersion 1, independent of the existing graph-store schema version' and rejects hypothetical legacy assessment converters. The proposed separate metadata namespace follows that boundary. [files: src/db/graph/store.ts, docs/epics/understand-changes-before-committing-E20261017670419c4/HLD.md]

findings.premise: The persisted attempt confidence enum preserves the sibling-owned answer contract.
findings.evidence: HLD sc4, owned by s3, defines AnswerSubmission.confidence as 'unsure' | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'. LLD §3.3 instead stores 'sure/unsure/unset'. Valid low/medium/high submissions cannot be represented faithfully: implementation would reject them or collapse the original confidence that S001/ac1 requires retaining. [files: docs/epics/understand-changes-before-committing-E20261017670419c4/HLD.md, docs/epics/understand-changes-before-committing-E20261017670419c4/DEF.md]
findings.action: Preserve the sc4 confidence values in submitted attempts. Represent an unanswered state separately if needed; do not replace the sibling-owned enum without an upstream contract amendment.

findings.premise: The existing transaction helper supports synchronous, atomic mutation callbacks with rollback on failure.
findings.evidence: Read the complete withWriteTxn implementation: it executes root.childTransaction(run), rejects thenable callback results, propagates transaction failures, and probes stalled writes for lost locks. This supports committing current/history/request changes together and returning a typed failure instead of partial success. [files: src/db/graph/store.ts]
findings.action: Keep all writes inside the synchronous callback and translate failures at the understanding RPC boundary.

findings.premise: All three S001 acceptance criteria have planned tests using an existing isolated persistence-test pattern.
findings.evidence: DEF S001/ac1 covers retained answers/confidence/progress/associations; ac2 covers unchanged delivery status and approvals; ac3 covers restart recovery without false passes. The LLD maps each to persistence, delivery-invariance, or recovery/contract tests. Existing store tests use mkdtempSync, setGraphStorePath, close/reopen, and withWriteTxn, providing the proposed isolation pattern. These are planned tests, not verified implementation results. [files: docs/epics/understand-changes-before-committing-E20261017670419c4/DEF.md, src/db/graph/__tests__/store.test.ts]
findings.action: Include every upstream confidence value in the round-trip fixtures after correcting the contract mismatch.
